one_line: Confirmation-first WebMCP action layer for screen-reader users.
what_it_does: Lets an NVDA user describe an action, discover or infer page tools, review one proposed call in an editable confirmation dialog, then execute and hear the result.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools and schema parity let the agent act without putting agent-only metadata into the accessibility tree; this is materially safer and more precise than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: PITCH and about text define WebMCP as the actuator while NVDA remains the interface.
Native tools, conservative inference, one-call confirmation, authorization extension, and parity tests are described.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent multi-part architecture and baseline/instrumented demo, but no video or product frames are submitted and the screenshot is packaging evidence only.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo are reported.
About text specifies extension, NVDA add-on, relay, demo routes, and parity testing.
No frame-sheet evidence.
impact_rationale: Screen-reader users face real friction with complex forms, and keeping the familiar accessible interface while adding bounded assistance addresses a specific high-value need.
impact_evidence: Explicit NVDA target audience and confirmation-first workflow.
Fictional permit workflow illustrates form complexity.
creativity_rationale: The indirect actuator model—agent reasoning outside the accessibility tree while the screen reader stays primary—is a novel, thoughtful interaction design.
creativity_evidence: About text explicitly frames the accessibility-tree problem and shared action definitions.
usability_note: Confirmation and editable calls are promising, but usability is not visually demonstrated.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame evidence; execution claims are largely unverified.
standouts: Strong accessibility-specific safety model and schema parity concept.
advance_reason: High-impact accessibility concept with substantial WebMCP leverage; advance despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: Voice or text appointment booking with clarification instead of guessing.

leverage_rationale: Typed slot search, booking, status tools and an in-flow clarification pause make agent booking substantially more reliable than navigating date pickers, though the underlying task remains UI-replicable.
leverage_evidence: Three registered tools with JSON schemas are described.
book_appointment explicitly pauses for missing patient name via requestUserInteraction.

D1 persistence for appointments and personal events is described.
Live demo reported alive.
impact_rationale: Appointment booking is a concrete, frequent barrier for elderly users and people uncomfortable with forms; the solution directly reduces that friction.
impact_evidence: Specific audience and five-field form/date-picker problem stated.
Visible availability confirmation supports the use case.
creativity_rationale: Conversational booking plus a page-native clarification handoff is a fresh synthesis, though appointment calendars are a known category.
creativity_evidence: requestUserInteraction is integrated into booking rather than bolted on as chat.
usability_note: Clear calendar and confirmation flow; voice input is an additional accessibility convenience.
standouts: Visible end-to-end availability confirmation and human clarification boundary.
advance_reason: Strong evidence-backed execution and meaningful agent-native booking workflow.
